reading1.passage:
Modern cities are changing quickly. The government has an important role in making cities safe and comfortable for their citizens. It must provide good services, improve public transport and develop better infrastructure. Roads, schools, hospitals and public transport are all important parts of city life.

The government also has a responsibility to support people who need help. One important area is employment. People need jobs to earn money and support their families. However, finding a good job is not always easy. A person with more experience may have more opportunities, but young people also need chances to enter the workforce.

Modern cities are also places where people can learn about science and new ideas. Scientific discovery can improve daily life. For example, new technology can make transport faster and communication easier. Governments and universities can support research and encourage young people to study science.

Another important part of city life is culture. Many cities attract tourists because of their history, food, buildings and festivals. Tourism can create jobs and bring money to local businesses. However, too many visitors can sometimes create problems.

One common problem is congestion. When there are too many cars and buses on the roads, people may spend a long time travelling. Better public transport and improved infrastructure can help reduce this problem.

A successful city therefore needs cooperation between the government, workers, businesses and citizens. Each group has a responsibility to help create a better place to live.

reading2.passage:
Cities are becoming larger and more connected, and this creates both opportunities and challenges. A modern city needs effective government and good planning if it wants to provide a high quality of life for its residents. Government decisions can influence employment, transport, education, scientific research and cultural activities.

One major responsibility of government is to develop suitable infrastructure. As the population of a city grows, roads, public transport, schools and other facilities must also improve. Without proper planning, cities may experience serious congestion, especially during the morning and evening rush hours. Long journeys can waste time and may also increase air pollution.

Public transport is one possible solution. If buses and trains are reliable, affordable and comfortable, more people may choose them instead of private cars. This can reduce the number of vehicles on the roads. However, transport improvements require investment, careful planning and cooperation between different organizations.

Another important issue is employment. A growing city can provide many new jobs, but workers need suitable skills and experience. Education and training can help people become more professional and adapt to changes in the labour market. Young workers may have less experience, but training programmes can give them a useful opportunity to develop their abilities.

Cities can also benefit from science and technological discovery. Universities and research centres can develop new solutions for transport, energy and public services. Scientific research can therefore contribute to both economic development and everyday life.

At the same time, cities should not forget their culture. Historic buildings, traditional food, festivals and local customs can attract tourists and create income for local communities. Tourism, however, must be managed carefully. A large number of visitors can put pressure on transport systems, public spaces and local services.

The future of a city depends on balance. Governments need to improve infrastructure while protecting cultural identity. Businesses need workers with useful skills, and citizens need to take responsibility for their communities. If these groups cooperate, cities can become more efficient, attractive and comfortable places to live.

listening.passage:
Many cities are growing quickly, and this creates new challenges for both the government and citizens. The government has an important responsibility to make sure that people have good public services and safe places to live.

One important area is infrastructure. Roads, buses and other public facilities must be improved when the population grows. Without good planning, cities can have serious congestion. People may spend a lot of time travelling to work or school.

Another issue is employment. A growing city can create new jobs, but workers need useful skills and experience. Young people can improve their chances of finding work through education and training.

Science also has an important role in modern cities. A new scientific discovery may provide better solutions for transport, energy or communication. Universities and research centres can help cities develop new ideas.

Cities also need to protect their culture. Historic buildings, traditional food and local festivals can attract tourists. Visitors can support local shops, hotels and restaurants. However, too many tourists may put pressure on transport and public services.

For this reason, a successful city needs cooperation. The government must plan carefully, businesses must provide employment, and citizens must share responsibility for their communities. With good planning, cities can become cleaner, safer and more comfortable places to live.
